subject: Commercial readiness + procurement path for BlueHarbor trial
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Kim Nguyen <k.nguyen@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Commercial readiness + procurement path for BlueHarbor trial

Hi Kim —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on procurement readiness before we spin up the pilot environment:

- Pilot scope: 3 developer seats, production-like inference on two internal models for feature testing (low concurrency).
- Pricing: estimate shown in the demo deck — we can convert to a 30-day trial quote.
- Procurement questions you raised: PO vs card, vendor onboarding, vendor terms for trial, and where budget lives internally.

Next steps I propose:
1) You share the vendor onboarding form / PO template if you want Redwood to fill it out (we can pre-populate).
2) Confirm whether procurement will issue a PO for the pilot or if card payment is preferred.
3) Identify the finance/budget owner and the signatory path (name, role, and email).
4) Quick follow-up meeting (15 min) with procurement if helpful — suggest Wed 5/5 or Thu 5/6.

I'll drop the draft vendor info and a one‑page mutual action plan after this thread. If procurement prefers, we can also route through marketplace procurement (AWS/Azure) — will need to know that up front.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

[Attachment: Redwood_Vendor_Profile.pdf (PDF)]

From: Kim Nguyen <k.nguyen@blueharbor.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@blueharbor.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 10:23:14 -0700
Subject: Re: Commercial readiness + procurement path for BlueHarbor trial

Hi Lauren —

Thanks for the recap. A few clarifications from procurement's side:  
1) For pilots under $25k we usually prefer purchasing card, but larger pilots go via PO. Can you confirm a firm trial spend estimate so we can flag the right path?
2) We have a standard vendor onboarding packet — attaching the PO template and onboarding checklist.
3) Our internal budget owner for innovation pilots is often Maya Rodriguez (cc'd from procurement); final signatory will be our VP of Finance if the spend goes > $50k.

Attaching: BlueHarbor_PO_Template.pdf, Vendor_Onboarding_Checklist.pdf

Can your team fill in the vendor packet and return? Also, does Redwood support a standard Net30/Net45 on pilot invoices or only upfront?

Thanks,
Kim Nguyen
Sr. Product Manager, Integrations
BlueHarbor Health
k.nguyen@blueharbor.com

[Attachment: BlueHarbor_PO_Template.pdf (PDF)]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Kim Nguyen <k.nguyen@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 13:08:42 -0700
Subject: Re: Commercial readiness + procurement path for BlueHarbor trial

Hi Kim —

Great, this is exactly what we needed. Quick answers and plan:  
- Pilot spend estimate: $9,800 for a 30-day pilot at the configuration we discussed (up to 100k tokens/day, low concurrency). This keeps it under your $25k card threshold.
- Payment options: we can accept card for the pilot. If you later convert to reserved capacity, we can provide invoicing terms (Net30/Net45) depending on legal and credit review. For trial/proof-of-value we typically take card to avoid onboarding friction.
- Marketplace: Redwood is available through the AWS Marketplace in some regions; if BlueHarbor prefers marketplace procurement we can route, but it typically adds ~7–10 business days to onboarding.

Action items from us:
- I will complete your Vendor_Onboarding_Form and return by EOD Wed 5/5.
- Ben (cc) will prepare a short mutual action plan and a copy of our standard trial SOW for your legal team.

Can you confirm the email for the budget owner and the preferred PO contact? If Maya is the budget owner, please confirm her email so we can include her on the mutual action plan. Also: any requirements for a W-9 or vendor W-8?

Thanks — happy to jump on a 15-min sync if procurement wants to run through the packet.

— Lauren
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

[Attachment: Redwood_Filled_Vendor_Profile_draft.pdf (will send Wed 5/5)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kim Nguyen <k.nguyen@blueharbor.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 09:11:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Commercial readiness + procurement path for BlueHarbor trial

Hi Kim —

Appreciate the context. Two quick notes from a commercial perspective:  
1) For pilots we usually recommend card to expedite the trial; we will proactively ship the vendor packet back populated to speed PO workflows if you later need it.
2) If BlueHarbor needs Net30/Net45 for production purchase, we can scope that in during conversion and start a credit review in parallel so there's no gap.

Lauren will send the populated packet. If procurement prefers marketplace procurement, please let us know and we'll connect you to our cloud partner lead.

If helpful, I'll join the short procurement sync to unblock the vendor setup.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

[Attachment: Commercial_Mutual_Action_Plan.docx]

Thanks — confirmed items below:  
- Pilot budget approved at $10k (card preferred for the pilot).
- Budget owner: Maya Rodriguez, Director of Innovation (m.rodriguez@blueharbor.com).
- Procurement will issue a PO for anything > $25k; for this pilot we will process via corporate card.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
